title: Publishing a repository is a separate choice
when: Project creation, clone, existing-folder adoption or later publication
need: A prepared Git repository can stay local. Skipping GitHub makes the publish prompt default to No — keep it local; a verified connection keeps Yes — publish to GitHub selected. Connecting GitHub does not require publishing every project. Clone and adoption share an explicit publication destination choice: read-only preserves fetching and disables pushes through Git pushurl; source writes state confirmed versus unverified access; Fork and Duplicate use supported owned destinations. Publication-required work refuses read-only destinations before lane preparation. Repeated setup reopens the same destination choice for a read-only project and preserves a configured writable project.
gap: JOURNEYS 4–5 currently makes pushing to GitHub sound mandatory. That edge should be reviewed against the supported keep-local path.
review: Source behavior only; installed wizard/agent clone/adoption and genuine remote completion remain owed by the single shared installer mission case.
